content: 1. Drug Interactions with Norethindrone: Elagolix: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. It is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor closely and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A4 substrates if co-administered. Encorafenib: This drug can both inhibit and induce CYP3A4, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing the efficacy of norethindrone. Use caution and monitor closely. Enzalutamide: This drug significantly decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during co-administration. Etravirine: This drug decreases norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Fedratinib: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Fexinidazole: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration due to the risk of adverse effects. Fosamprenavir: This drug has a variable effect on norethindrone levels. Use non-hormonal contraception as hormonal methods may be unreliable. Fosphenytoin: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary, and use additional contraception methods. Idelalisib: This drug increases norethindrone levels by strongly inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Iloperidone: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely for increased plasma levels of CYP3A4 substrates. Indinavir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Insulin (various types): Norethindrone may reduce the efficacy of insulin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor glucose tolerance closely. Istradefylline: This drug increases norethindrone levels at higher doses (40 mg/day). Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Ivosidenib: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Lamotrigine: Norethindrone decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Monitor plasma concentrations closely. Lenacapavir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely for potential adverse reactions. Lesinurad: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional non-hormonal contraception methods. Letermovir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Lorlatinib: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: This combination decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during co-administration. Maraviroc: Norethindrone increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely for toxicity. Mavacamten: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative contraception methods unaffected by CYP450 induction. Metformin: Norethindrone may reduce the efficacy of metformin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. Mifepristone: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and consider backup contraception methods. Mitotane: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Nafcillin: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use non-hormonal contraception during therapy. Nelfinavir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Nemolizumab: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP enzyme activity. Monitor closely and adjust dosages as needed. Phenobarbital: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Phenytoin: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Primidone: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Ribociclib: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely. Rifabutin: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Rifampin: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use non-hormonal contraception during therapy. Rifapentine: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Ritonavir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Rucaparib: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Adjust dosages of CYP3A4 substrates as needed. Rufinamide: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Siltuximab: This drug may restore CYP450 activity by inhibiting IL-6. Use caution with narrow therapeutic index drugs. Stiripentol: This drug can both inhibit and induce CYP3A4, leading to variable effects. Monitor closely and adjust dosages as needed. Sugammadex: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by receptor binding competition. Use additional contraception methods for 7 days after administration. Tazemetostat: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Tecovirimat: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Tesamorelin: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative contraception methods. Tipranavir: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Topiramate: This drug decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Tucatinib: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration unless necessary. Voriconazole: This drug increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Precautions and Contraindications: Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable when co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors. Use additional non-hormonal contraception methods. Norethindrone may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the efficacy of insulin or metformin. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. Contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to the drug or its components, hormone-sensitive malignancies, hepatic impairment, or undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding. Discontinue therapy if pregnancy occurs, as early pregnancy loss may result. Monitor for signs of gallbladder disease, hypertension, or uterine fibroid complications during therapy. 3. Breastfeeding Considerations: Norethindrone and its metabolites may be present in breast milk and could reduce milk production. Use caution in breastfeeding women. 4. General Recommendations: Advise patients to use reliable contraception methods unaffected by CYP450 interactions, such as intrauterine devices or condoms, during and after therapy.
